title: Beryllium — curated atomic gas supplement, 2026-10-06
body:
# Beryllium — curated atomic gas supplement, 2026-10-06

Stage status: IMPLEMENTED. Actual terminal verification is recorded in the linked batch receipt. Full MAT scientific and standalone-image acceptance remains PARTIAL.

## Existing owners and reconciliation

MAT:0004 remains Beryllium. The [unchanged master](../../records/0004-Beryllium-Be/data/structured/0004-Beryllium-Be.yaml) declares neutral MAT:0004:ATOM:Be at /states/0, separately from MAT:0004:PHASE:HCP at /bulk_reference/phase. Existing isotope, HCP bulk, nuclear, safety and compound-specific BeO property owners retain their scope. The [table manifest](../../records/0004-Beryllium-Be/data/structured/0004-Beryllium-Be-Table-Manifest.yaml) retains its eight authored entries; the [graph manifest](../../records/0004-Beryllium-Be/data/structured/0004-Beryllium-Be-Graph-Manifest.yaml) retains nine reserved graphs. Graph008 BeO conductivity and graph 009 pressure-phase map are not elemental gas heat capacity. Explicit reviewed table 10/graph 10 are added without renumbering table 009 or altering existing reservations. Original bytes and complete authored prefixes are preserved.

## Primary source and bounded acceptance

The [NIST gas-only page](https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7440417&Units=SI&Mask=1) identifies neutral Be, CAS7440-41-7, InChI=1S/Be. One Chase (1998) GAS fit covers **2741.437–6000 K**, on **mol Be** basis; its comment reports September 1983 review. **SRC-000511** is a new species-specific source in the [existing registry](../../data/registries/sources.yaml), distinct from isotope, bulk, melting/boiling and BeO references. No equivalent existing WebBook gas source was found. It is not independent corroboration. The [main snapshot](../../data/catalog/sources/nist-thermochemistry-0004-2026-10-06.html.txt) and [publisher snapshot](../../data/catalog/sources/nist-thermochemistry-0004-2026-10-06-table.html.txt) retain exact original bytes and SHA-256 hashes. The [publisher table](https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7440417&Units=SI&Mask=1&Type=JANAFG&Table=on) supplies 34 rounded Cp/entropy/enthalpy-increment comparisons; all passed. All 101 accepted samples are finite and positive, with numerical dH/dT and dS/dT checks passing.

The first publisher temperature is printed as 2741., nominally below the fit. Its printed-format cell 2740.5–2741.5 K contains the exact minimum 2741.437 K, where all three outputs match at printed precision. The [evaluation index](../../data/catalog/thermochemistry-evaluation-index.json) preserves the raw row and explicit calculation_temperature_K resolution; the per-record owner retains the explanatory note and source links. The accepted CSV starts at 2741.437 K. No accepted calculation evaluates 2741 K, widens fit validity or treats printed rounding as physical uncertainty.

H(T)-H(298.15 K) retains its published reference offset; it does not authorize evaluating this high-temperature gas fit at 298.15 K or construct a phase-transition path. A separately retained [condensed-phase page](https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7440417&Units=SI&Mask=2) contains one liquid and two solid fits, reviewed privately only. None is bound to the neutral atomic gas owner. Condensed integration requires applicable phase/state binding and source review. Applied sample pressure, isotope proportions and coefficient uncertainty/covariance remain UNKNOWN. Molecular spin-isomer populations do not apply to a monatomic species. No Be2 properties, equilibrium fractions, latent heats, boiling point, phase diagram or arbitrary-pressure response are inferred.

## Implemented outputs and validation

The [reader chapter](../../records/0004-Beryllium-Be/0004-Beryllium-Be-Thermochemistry.md), [structured evaluation](../../records/0004-Beryllium-Be/data/structured/0004-Beryllium-Be-NIST-Thermochemistry.yaml), [readable table](../../records/0004-Beryllium-Be/tables/0004-Beryllium-Be-TABLE-010-Thermodynamic-Functions.md), [CSV](../../records/0004-Beryllium-Be/tables/0004-Beryllium-Be-TABLE-010-Thermodynamic-Functions.csv) and [SVG chart](../../records/0004-Beryllium-Be/graphs/0004-Beryllium-Be-GRAPH-010-Heat-Capacity.svg) share the same retained source, state, units, range and explicit unknown context. The existing curated GAS-only importer, append guards, slot checks, numerical validation and native plot generator are reused; no production-code or schema change is needed. Native preview received actual visual inspection. This supplemental chart earns zero standalone A/B panel credit.

The [batch receipt](../../data/quality/thermal-beryllium-batch-2026-10-06.json) records exact changed files, source/artifact hashes, preservation, executed tests, terminal results, migrations and repository state. Source-transcription and arithmetic checks are not independent calorimetry or experimental replication. Global totals are 39 thermal owners / 138 fits / 13,938 rows / 71 bounded thermal source gaps and 267 supplemental elemental charts. All 119 canonical identities remain represented. All 143 master tasks, 4,248 confirmed-domain reviews and 2,587 standalone confirmed-element panels remain pending; zero elements are certified fully advanced. The [existing selector](../../data/research/mat-update-review.json) and [MAT TODO](../../data/quality/MAT-TODO.json) retain those boundaries.

## Next executable requirement

Audit authored Boron 0005 and its applicable primary thermochemical sources. Neutral MAT:0005:ATOM:B is at /atomic_states/0; preserve its solid allotropes and B2/B12 structural motifs as separate species/state contexts. Accept a gas-only atomic supplement under the existing contract, or first extend applicable phase/state bindings for condensed fits. Graph slots 001–010 are reserved: graph 011 is first free. Table 010 is free (table 009 is also free). Use reviewed asset_slots {table:10,graph:11} only after repeating both physical and manifest collision checks. SRC-000064 already owns the Boron WebBook work for electron-affinity/ion-energetics; preserve it and link any accepted dated gas retrieval through same_work_as: SRC-000064. Recompute the next unreserved source ID after the Beryllium accession. Preserve the master, manifests and authored bytes, then continue 0006–0012 individually. Universal atomic-child projection, 71 bounded thermal source gaps, transport/dynamics/domain acceptance, source metadata/documentation and remaining standalone images remain pending. Source/state/table/chart acceptance precedes illustrations; MAT remains PARTIAL.

sources.scope_note: Species-specific neutral gas evaluation; distinct from the retained Beryllium isotope, HCP bulk, melting/boiling and BeO compound thermal-property references. No existing equivalent WebBook gas accession found. Publisher calculations are not independent corroboration.
sources.scope: The exact publisher species is Be with InChI=1S/Be, not Be2, Be ions or an equilibrium vapor mixture. One mole of the source species is one mole of Be atoms. No molecular factor of two applies. The gas-only response supplies one fit for 2741.437–6000 K. A separate retained condensed-phase diagnostic contains one LIQUID fit and two SOLID fits. Those fits are not imported, relabelled, or bound to the neutral atomic GAS state. No gas evaluation below the source minimum 2741.437 K is justified. The retained source limits do not themselves establish a boiling point, a gas stability boundary or a pressure-dependent phase boundary. Existing Be isotope records and atomic-weight data retain separate scope. No isotope-specific gas properties or numeric isotope abundances are inferred from this elemental fit or its listed molecular weight. The Shomate equations contain no pressure variable. Applied pressure, arbitrary-pressure EOS and phase diagrams are not inferred. Separate source entropy reference-pressure labels belong to those original data only. No Be/Be2 equilibrium fraction, dimer dissociation, ionisation fraction, charge-state mixture or molecular nuclear-spin population is calculated or assigned. Fit boundaries from separate phases and enthalpy reference offsets are retained as reported and are not a constructed phase-transition path or latent-heat calculation. Coefficient uncertainty and covariance are unreported. Printed-temperature cells, output rounding and numerical derivative residuals are source-format/software checks, not physical uncertainty. Independent transcription arithmetic against publisher values and positive samples within the fit do not establish experimental replication, new calorimetry, complete Beryllium thermophysics or element completion.
sources.reference: Chase, M.W., Jr. (1998), NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables, Fourth Edition. Fit comment: Data last reviewed in September, 1983.
